text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Each dot is one arm in one control at one shift size: its error gain over B0, net of its gain on the unshifted data, divided by the oracle's gain (0: none, 1: all of it). The oracle is B0 given the true shift factor, the most any lag feature could gain. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months and a seed. Dashed lines: no gain (0) and the oracle's gain (1). A pair is shown only where the oracle's own 99% interval excludes zero. In the plant-steps control, 0 of 10 shares have an interval wholly above zero.'
text.tspan: Each dot is one arm in one control at one shift size: its error gain over B0, net of its gain on the unshifted
data, divided by the oracle's gain (0: none, 1: all of it). The oracle is B0 given the true shift factor, the most
any lag feature could gain. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months and a seed.
Dashed lines: no gain (0) and the oracle's gain (1). A pair is shown only where the oracle's own 99% interval
excludes zero. In the plant-steps control, 0 of 10 shares have an interval wholly above zero.

text.aria-label: Title text 'A control is a planted-loss test: the forecasts are re-fitted on a synthetic target in which measured power is cut by the shift (5% or 10%). In the month-level control, the cut applies in 9 of the 18 scored months and a random half of the others. In the plant-steps control, each plant's power is cut for a random 4 to 12 weeks. An arm's standing gain on the unshifted data is subtracted so that it is not counted as recovery. All rows are post hoc: written after the first run's results were known. Arms. B0: the baseline with no lag. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). AN: the analogue ensemble: the mean, clear-sky index and spread of the power, rescaled by clear-sky irradiance, on the 5 of the last 30 days whose forecast clear-sky index was closest to the target's. W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same hour over the last 7 whole days. TF: the 30-day ratio of power to forecast irradiance (the transfer ratio). PC: the 7-day ratio of power to the satellite irradiance of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS), and the 30-day ratio of CAMS to forecast irradiance.'
text.tspan: A control is a planted-loss test: the forecasts are re-fitted on a synthetic target in which measured power is cut by the
shift (5% or 10%). In the month-level control, the cut applies in 9 of the 18 scored months and a random half of the others.
In the plant-steps control, each plant's power is cut for a random 4 to 12 weeks. An arm's standing gain on the unshifted
data is subtracted so that it is not counted as recovery.
All rows are post hoc: written after the first run's results were known.
Arms. B0: the baseline with no lag. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. L1: B0 plus the power at the
same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast).
AN: the analogue ensemble: the mean, clear-sky index and spread of the power, rescaled by clear-sky irradiance, on the 5 of
the last 30 days whose forecast clear-sky index was closest to the target's. W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same
hour over the last 7 whole days. TF: the 30-day ratio of power to forecast irradiance (the transfer ratio). PC: the 7-day
